in_arabic.name: إلاءف
in_arabic.long_meaning: الإلاءف: اللطف والمحبة، المعنی اللطافة في النفس والقلب، والمحبة التي لا تنقطع. یأتی من الجذر اللطیف، ویلقى إشارة إلى النفس الرفیعة والطبیعة الإنسانیة. في الإسلام، یعد الإلاءف إحدى صفات الله تعالى، وینسب إلى المؤمنین الجدد الذين یعاملون الآخرین باللطف والمحبة.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ilaaf holds a unique cultural position in the Islamic community as it signifies the idea of ascent, elevation and reaching greater heights. In various Islamic texts and folklore, Ilaaf is an angel or a spiritual guide that helps believers navigate their spiritual journey towards enlightenment and self-improvement. The name is also used in Sufism, the mystical branch of Islam, to describe the ultimate state of union with the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: Ilaaf holds immense spiritual significance for Muslims as it embodies the idea of striving for spiritual growth and closeness to Allah. Through various spiritual practices and acts of worship, Muslims seek to ascend to a higher spiritual plane and attain the presence of Allah. The name Ilaaf serves as a constant reminder of this eternal quest for self-improvement and divine closeness. In surah Ar-Robbiya, Allah Almighty says "Whoever desires the Hereafter, and We will give him an increase.” (Ad-Dhaariyaat: 54) This verse emphasizes the importance of striving for the Hereafter and the constant effort to seek Allah's pleasure, symbolically represented by the name Ilaaf.
